commits.message: Match the intended refusal in the rehearsal profile tests
Carry the release-age exemption into the boundary consumer

Add the preprod-rehearsal deployment profile

A Preprod profile for rehearsing the public deploy with low bonds. Every
value equals preprod-public's except the economics and the pooled DA bond
amounts, which equal preprod-testing's under its bounded-acceptance-v1
schedule, so maturity, dispute, operator shift and every DA window match
the public release while bonds stay cheap. preprod-testing stays the
selected profile and is unchanged.

The rehearsal is classed with the public profiles everywhere except
economics: the production allow-list and commit-event depth rules, the
retained-DA transport requirement, the public timing rules, release
provenance and watcher release authoring, the blueprint classification
registry, public HTTP/TLS listen, readiness and database-error redaction,
the opener margin, and the release image and blueprint-rebuild scripts.

The profile-name and profile-class tables move to
deployment-profile-names.mjs, and the generator now emits
PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE_NAMES so core, node and watcher read one
public-class helper instead of comparing names. The new module is listed
wherever the generator inputs are (CI paths, preflight FULL_RUN, traced
refusal inputs, the interactive emulator fixture).

The generated profile table's size cap rises to its new line count: it
holds one literal per profile.

Tests compare the loaded profiles rather than pinning numbers: the
rehearsal is preprod-public with preprod-testing's economics and DA bond,
is held to every production rule preprod-public is, and generates its own
Aiken environment.

Bump Lucid to 0.8.9 and uplc to 0.5.3, and drop HarmonicLabs

uplc 0.5.3 decodes a tag 102 Plutus Data constructor (index 128 and up)
in the indefinite form, the spelling Lucid's Data.to writes. Before it,
the evaluator's decoder left that pair's break unread, so the enclosing
list ended there and a sibling value after the constructor broke the
transaction decode: local evaluation of any script transaction whose
redeemer or inline datum held such a value failed. tx-completion.test.ts
pins it: a script spend whose redeemer and inline datum are
Constr(0, [Constr(128, []), 5]) completes and submits.

utils 0.3.0, which lucid 0.8.9 depends on, applies script parameters
through the uplc wasm instead of @harmoniclabs/uplc and plutus-data.
That retires the two utils@0.2.6>@harmoniclabs overrides, the utils
patch that adapted applyParamsToScript to UPLC 2's encodeUPLC, and the
sdk's cbor and crypto dependencies, which were there only so Lucid's
harmonic copy matched the sdk's. No @harmoniclabs package is left in
the lockfile; the first case of lucid-parameterization-resolution.test.ts
now checks that none resolves from any workspace package, from Lucid or
from Lucid's own packages.

pnpm 11 holds a package back for a day after it is published.
@lucid-evolution/* are releases we cut ourselves, so the workspace
exempts them (minimumReleaseAgeExclude). A frozen install with a clean
HOME passes with the exemption and is refused without it.

pnpmDepsHash follows the lockfile.

Check a signed public release as public listen does before reporting it

sign-deployment-release verified only the release signature and the watcher's reopen. A public release it reported as signed could still be refused by public listen: provenance without a node, Postgres or ingress image signed cleanly, and no public node could start from it. The command now opens a public release with authenticatePublicHttpRelease, with the manifest id and the provenance's source revision and role images as the expected identities, and refuses the release otherwise. The old test's mounted-registry check computed the expected digest from the file it checked, so it could never fail; it is gone, and a preprod-public-release Vitest project signs a public release and has the real public listen check accept it and refuse a changed revision, an edited classification reason and another key's trust roots.

programCommitments was signed as typed, so a mistyped commitment produced a release that verified. The command derives computation-thread-policy-v1 from the manifest's computation-thread policy (the derivation the devnet release uses, now shared) and refuses a supplied value that differs. The field stays in the release input, which e2e-stack shares and binds into its intent digest; it may be empty.

A refusal after the output directory was created left it behind, so a retry failed with EEXIST. Any refusal now removes the directory the call created. Tests cover the retry and --funding-payment-key-hash, and the docs scope the external-roots rule to public listen and name the profile generation step.

Build a preprod-public test blueprint and let the registry fixture use it

A test that signs a public release and opens it as public listen does needs the preprod-public profile compiled. The emulator-profile mechanism already selects a profile inside one Vitest project and builds a separately stamped blueprint for it; preprod-public-profile.js applies it to preprod-public under onchain/aiken/build/preprod-public. CI builds it once in test-blueprints and the node tools job restores it under MIDGARD_REQUIRE_PREBUILT_BLUEPRINTS, as the interactive and curated blueprints are.

The genuine deployment registry fixture failed under a public profile: the node's member list also checks the members against the unused-validator census from MIDGARD_BLUEPRINT_CLASSIFICATION_FILE, which the fixture had not built yet. It now takes the members from the SDK directly (the same list without that check) and, for a public profile, mounts its census in that variable while the manifest is built. Testing profiles behave as before.

Refuse every @harmoniclabs import in the demo workspace

Midgard's own code no longer imports any @harmoniclabs package: the Plutus Data, constant and term classes and the Flat encoder are owned in midgard-validation, and builtins run through the pinned aiken wasm. A no-restricted-imports pattern now refuses @harmoniclabs/* in every block that configures the rule, so the dependency cannot come back through a stray import.

no-recursive-plutus-data drops its @harmoniclabs branches (the recursive plutus-data codecs, the plutus-machine allow-list and harmonic Cbor), which named packages that are no longer installed; it keeps cborg and Lucid Data.from/Data.to. Its fixtures and docs/agents/lint-rules.md follow.

Build the fee-sensitive Lucid fixture with an owned Flat encoder

The static-completion fixture built its fee-threshold script with @harmoniclabs/uplc, reached through @lucid-evolution/utils. That package is leaving the dependency graph once utils applies parameters through the aiken wasm, so the fixture now writes its program with a small Flat encoder of its own that covers the terms and constants it uses. Its output is byte-identical to harmonic compileUPLC for the fixture program at fourteen thresholds (zero, signs, 7-bit group edges, 64- and 70-bit values) and for a 600-byte bytestring that needs chunking.

Add a release signing command for the deployment release

sign-deployment-release signs a finalized deployment with the release key
named by the existing release input and writes, into a new directory, every
file public listen and the watcher verify: the signed authority, its trust
roots, the rule and funding bundles, the manifest and deployment info, the
blueprint, and the provenance, parameter registry and classification when
supplied. It reuses the watcher's release authoring and checks the result
with the shared release verifier against the written trust roots.

Tests sign with temporary keys and check the output with the core release
verifier, the node's mounted registry check and the watcher's authority
loader, and that a tampered binding and another key's signature are refused.

Tighten the HarmonicLabs-migrated tests after review

- reserve-payout evaluation context: the control now re-encodes every
  output through CML, the path each mutation takes, instead of an empty
  replacement that was equal by construction.
- cek-cost parameter names: probe the 64/65 boundary and 2^20, and give
  arity-6 ChooseData one vector of distinct sizes.
- Flat encode differential: state what agreement with the crate proves;
  the crate normalises Data, so it catches non-minimal output, and the
  program-to-bytes mapping is anchored by the reader's vector tables.
- real minting policy: refusals assert error_kind 2 (failed within
  budget) as well as ok false; tq-05 records the question as settled.

Drop HarmonicLabs from midgard-validation and midgard-node

Nothing in either package imports it any more. The lockfile loses only
the removed entries and the packages no one else needs; pnpmDepsHash
follows it. The Lucid resolution test no longer compares the Harmonic
instances Lucid's utils resolve with midgard-validation's, which has
none; it still pins them to 2.x and to the SDK's CBOR and crypto.

Migrate midgard-node tests off HarmonicLabs

The real minting-policy evaluation test runs the policies through the
pinned aiken evaluator (eval_program_raw) instead of the HarmonicLabs
machine, which re-enables the hub-oracle case its lessThanByteString
defect had forced off. The reserve-payout mutants splice replacement
items into the signed bytes instead of reparsing and re-encoding the
whole transaction. Fixtures build programs with the owned term classes
and Flat encoder.

Name builtins in validation generators from the owned table

The golden generators take builtin names, arities and force counts from
midgard-validation's own tables, which match aiken's textual syntax, and
build programs with the owned term classes and Flat encoder. Every
generator's --check output is unchanged.

Migrate midgard-validation tests off HarmonicLabs

Builtins are named from an owned table of aiken's textual builtin names,
programs are written by the owned Flat encoder, and every independent
oracle that was HarmonicLabs is now the pinned aiken uplc evaluator or
CML: the Flat encoder differential re-encodes through the uplc crate, the
BLS expression oracle runs through eval_program_raw, the Data-tree
integer oracle decodes with CML PlutusData, and the fuzz oracle unwraps
compiled code with the midgard-core CBOR reader. Non-canonical Data
spellings are spliced into owned Flat bytes by a test helper.

The cost differential is deleted: the per-parameter test checks every
coefficient against aiken by name, and its refusals move into the cost
unit test.
Refresh the Nix pnpm dependency hash for the uplc 0.5.2 lockfile
